orb mercenary.name: Orb (Mercenary)
orb mercenary.species: Human mutate further augmented by the Watcher's eye
orb mercenary.origin: ===Early Life=== The Orb was born with a head in the form of a giant eye. Due to this deformity, he was neglected by his mother, and was eventually abandoned at an early age. He was raised in a freak show, where he was forced to sleep in cages and eat cat food. The Orb grew up being laughed at and mocked, and stayed a virgin until he was thirty-seven, when he paid for the experience. He wouldn't be able to speak for a long time, before he learned he could just make squishy sounds. ===Caretaker=== Some time later, he ended up becoming a mercenary, and was hired by Daniel Ketch to serve the angel Zadkiel alongside Blackout, Death Ninja, and Doghead. Together, they tried to kill Caretaker, a former adviser to Ketch. However, during the attack, the Orb accidentally damaged his eye after triggering a trap inside Caretaker's home, launching a wooden plank lined with nails into his head. Orb was taken to the South Nashville Prison Hospital, where he received treatment for his trauma. thumb|left ===Heaven's on Fire=== After recovering, the Orb was broken out of prison by Blackout and Deacon, who wanted him to serve Zadkiel's "task force" of Ghost Rider foes. Alongside Vengeance, the Orb attacked the gateway to Heaven, but was confronted by the Gun Nuns. He was later knocked out by Daniel Ketch while running and screaming for being shot in his left hand, seemingly losing three of his fingers. ===Time and Orblings=== Orb later returned to his life of crimes and formed a group of robbers, called the Orblings. While trying to rob a bank searching for jewels, was defeated by Spider-Man and Wolverine, before time diamonds scattered the three of them across the timeline. He experienced an alternate life where he was a muscle bound gun toting monster before being pulled back by the Minutemen. He was last seen being led away bemoaning having been reset to the regular timeline. ===Original Sin=== The Orb began having numerous dreams in which he observed the Watcher's base, what could've been a manifestation of his extra-sensory abilities. He contacted Doctor Midas, and offered to make a deal with him to rob the Watcher. When he, Midas and the Exterminatrix arrived to the Moon, they attacked the Watcher's citadel. As he was repelling Midas' Mindless Ones, the villains stole his armory. During the fight, the Orb envied Uatu's power and shot him so he would "never see anything again." The blast only left the Watcher unconscious, but it was enough for the Orb to take advantage of that and remove his left eye. Back on Earth, the eye's influence caused numerous Mindless Ones in possession of him to radically change, develop thoughts and evolve. After one of the Mindless Ones escaped the Orb's lair and committed suicide following a battle against the Avengers, the heroes began investigating the connection between the Mindless One's behavior and the death of Uatu. thumb|right|Unleashing a million secrets When The Orb was finally pinned down, he was confronted by numerous heroes, and activated the eye, unleashing the secrets of the Watcher. He was then apprehended and taken into custody in the Avengers Tower, from where he was freed by the Punisher and Doctor Strange so he could lead them to the eye, which had been stolen. The Orb took them to a secret satellite, where Punisher and Strange discovered other heroes who were working for the same person, Nick Fury. Fury took the Orb and tortured him so he could learn how to activate the other eye of the Watcher, the right one Fury had in his possession. The procedure also enhanced the Orb's powers, and he was able to defeat the heroes in the satellite and get back to the Moon, where Nick Fury also was, so he could see the Watcher's last secret. The Orb took one of the eyes from Fury, and it bonded with him, developing the obsession to watch different types of events when he returned to Earth. The Orb decided to take up the Watcher's job, albeit in his own twisted way. In addition to observing events more closely, the Orb, while claiming to abide to a rule of non-interference, considered it was acceptable to push forward the development of events he assumed would help people achieve their full potential, including pushing the actions of murderers and madmen. ===Deadpool & the Mercs for Money=== When Deadpool and the Mercs for Money sold a Rigellian Recorder seemingly capable of foretelling the future, the Orb, claiming that no one should have this kind of power, tried to kill them before they could delivery the robot to its new owner, the Ozarks Kingpin, but failed. ===Blood in the Aether=== When Doctor Strange was targeted by several of his enemies following the invasion of the Empirikul, the Orb got hold of him and took him hostage in his taxi. Having seen Strange's "sins," the Orb wanted to assist Strange in confronting them, namely the creature known as Mister Misery. However, the confrontation between Doctor Strange and Mister Misery was interrupted by the appearance of Baron Mordo,

The blast only left the Watcher unconscious, but it was enough for the Orb to take advantage of that and remove his left eye. Back on Earth, the eye's influence caused numerous Mindless Ones in possession of him to radically change, develop thoughts and evolve. After one of the Mindless Ones escaped the Orb's lair and committed suicide following a battle against the Avengers, the heroes began investigating the connection between the Mindless One's behavior and the death of Uatu. thumb|right|Unleashing a million secrets When The Orb was finally pinned down, he was confronted by numerous heroes, and activated the eye, unleashing the secrets of the Watcher. He was then apprehended and taken into custody in the Avengers Tower, from where he was freed by the Punisher and Doctor Strange so he could lead them to the eye, which had been stolen. The Orb took them to a secret satellite, where Punisher and Strange discovered other heroes who were working for the same person, Nick Fury. Fury took the Orb and tortured him so he could learn how to activate the other eye of the Watcher, the right one Fury had in his possession. The procedure also enhanced the Orb's powers, and he was able to defeat the heroes in the satellite and get back to the Moon, where Nick Fury also was, so he could see the Watcher's last secret. The Orb took one of the eyes from Fury, and it bonded with him, developing the obsession to watch different types of events when he returned to Earth. The Orb decided to take up the Watcher's job, albeit in his own twisted way. In addition to observing events more closely, the Orb, while claiming to abide to a rule of non-interference, considered it was acceptable to push forward the development of events he assumed would help people achieve their full potential, including pushing the actions of murderers and madmen. ===Deadpool & the Mercs for Money=== When Deadpool and the Mercs for Money sold a Rigellian Recorder seemingly capable of foretelling the future, the Orb, claiming that no one should have this kind of power, tried to kill them before they could delivery the robot to its new owner, the Ozarks Kingpin, but failed. ===Blood in the Aether=== When Doctor Strange was targeted by several of his enemies following the invasion of the Empirikul, the Orb got hold of him and took him hostage in his taxi. Having seen Strange's "sins," the Orb wanted to assist Strange in confronting them, namely the creature known as Mister Misery. However, the confrontation between Doctor Strange and Mister Misery was interrupted by the appearance of Baron Mordo,

orb neo.name: Orb (Neo)
orb neo.origin: Nothing is known about Orb, save that he was a member of the Neo's Guardian Clan who retained his powers after the Decimation when many other did not. Hearing of the birth of the Messiah-child, the Clan leader, Stare, led the powered members of the Clan in an attack on the X-Men in hopes of receiving answers. Orb aided Stare in taking Kavita Rao hostage, and later battled Mercury and Psylocke. However, the Evolutionaries arrived and declared the Neo a genetic dead end. When Stare attacked the lead Evolutionary, the Evolutionary destroyed the entire Guardian Clan from the inside out with a thought, and the rest of the planet's Neo population soon followed.

Rather than actually become super-heroes, they posed as a Fantastic Four-style group while secretly committing crimes that events would conspire to be blamed on Spider-Man. order heroes reborn.name: Order (Heroes Reborn)
order heroes reborn.origin: K and O are cosmic beings who are embodiments of chaos and order (although they would later tell Proteus that they were in fact two ordinary people). K and O were tasked with determining if the Heroes Reborn reality was salvageable or if it needed to be destroyed. Due to their embryonic nature they accidentally destroyed Paris, France when they manifested on Counter Earth. They later joined the Young Allies even though they had not rendered their judgement on the fate of that earth. It was later revealed K and O were trying to prevent an anomaly from devouring Counter Earth and that their destruction of Paris served as a temporary cork to keep the anomaly at bay. K and O revealed that the people of Paris had been reanimated as ghosts but K and O would not allow them to move on lest the anomaly be released. Mach-3 of the Thunderbolts chose to end their suffering but as a result the anomaly was released and empowered Koyami Sazaki. Koyami Sazaki as Anomaly defeated K and O but later was defeated by the Thunderbolts and sucked into the breach. Later Proteus in Morph's body convinced K and O to pass judgement against Counter Earth but the Exiles and Young Allies saved Counter Earth.

orelem.name: Orelem
orelem.origin: Circa 9,000 BC, Orelem was the leader of the Sera Thet tribe, in the village of Sera Thet. Sera Thet was one of many villages that the barbarians of Skar-Ka warred against, allegedly raping and pillaging the Sera Thet for ages. The tribe was joined by time-displaced "Brighthair" (Namorita/Kymaera), who tried to help them without endangering the course of history. She spied on the Skar-Ka, and discovered that their warlord Attumacht had invented a weapon combining a club and an axe, which ensured technological superiority over the Sera Thet. Kymaera decided to train them, diverted tools into weapons, in order for them to repel the Skar-Ka, only to discover horrified that Orelem intended to wipe out the Skar-Ka entirely. Kymaera broke out the fighting, and forced Orelem and Attumacht to consider their respective strengths and weaknesses, and realize their mutual interest self-preservation by working together, bringing them together. The Skarka endured into the Modern Age.
powers: Atlantean Physiology

orestez natchios.name: Orestez Natchios
orestez natchios.origin: Orestez was the older brother of Elektra Natchios by many years. He saw his father's embarrassment as his mother became increasingly flirtatious and presumably promiscuous with many men. When she became pregnant, Orestez's disdain for his mother led him to plan her murder and that of the bastard she presumably carried. Orestez was shamed to learn that not only was his father caught in the assassination attempt, but his baby sister was saved from their dying mother's womb and confirmed to be Hugo's child as well. Orestez was willingly exiled from the family estate, and had little to no contact with his father and baby sister in the following years. Decades later he was killed by the Punisher.

organo mechanic nexus iterated techno ra.origin: Upon finding his way into the Prime Universe, the Maker attempted to recreate the artificial intelligence named City in it, but due to this being a universe with natural laws more flamboyant than those of his native reality, he ended up creating a flamboyant new version of the A.I. instead. It dubbed itself O.M.N.I.T.R.O.N.I.C.U.S. (short for Organo-Mechanic Nexus-Iterated Techno-Radical Organizational Networked Intelligent Computer Unity System). O.M.N.I.T.R.O.N.I.C.U.S. later joined W.H.I.S.P.E.R., an organization the Maker strengthened with remnants of the dissolute Advanced Idea Mechanics; and the New Revengers, a team of supervillains gathered by the Maker to directly confront the New Avengers team assembled by Avengers Idea Mechanics. When the New Revengers attacked Avenger Base Two, O.M.N.I.T.R.O.N.I.C.U.S. was designated to exterminate Roberto da Costa, leader of Avengers Idea Mechanics. During the mission, however, the main computer where it was housed was destroyed by S.H.I.E.L.D. alongside W.H.I.S.P.E.R. HQ, resulting in its deactivation. The Maker eventually recovered a wrist unit from the wreckage and reactivated O.M.N.I.T.R.O.N.I.C.U.S.. With its assistance, the Maker tried to kidnap the President of the United States, but that plan was thwarted by da Costa and Warlock, the latter of whom caged O.M.N.I.T.R.O.N.I.C.U.S. in an imitation of Air Force One's system.
aliases: Master of the "Mechano-Force" The Omni-Computer Omnitronicus Overlord of the "Robo-Sapiens"

orikal.name: Orikal
orikal.origin: Orikal is an immensely powerful being from another universe. At some point, Orikal became the secret guardian of the Chalice of Ruins, a powerful talisman that could potentially be used to obtain the power of all-prevailing death. Orikal hid the chalice within himself as part of his being. Later, after having been entrusted with the Map of All-Ending, Odin somehow learned that Orikal possessed the chalice. Although the existence of these items was not to be discussed, Odin chose to whisper to his son Thor that he had sworn to protect the map with his life and that the chalice was in the possession of Orikal. ===Slave of the Rock Trolls=== In the modern age, Orikal wandered into the Earth-616 universe and, disoriented, was captured by Geirrodur, King of Trolls, who imprisoned him in a sea of fire from which he could not escape. Geirrodur used Orikal for information and for knowledge of advanced weaponry. Using this knowledge, Geirrodur was almost successful in conquering Asgard until Thor and Sif encountered Orikal, learned that he was being held prisoner and freed him. Once freed, Orikal immediately departed, leaving the weapons he had created for the Trolls powerless. Years later, Orikal somehow once again became a slave to Geirrodur and was again held captive in the Troll Kingdom, a fact that Thor somehow learned. After Asgard was laid waste and Thor was unable to travel to it, he sought out Orikal to ask what had happened. When Orikal refused to answer because his missing master had not freed him to speak of such events, an angered Thor was about to unleash his power when Marnot appeared. After Marnot told Thor about the Dark Gods and the long-ago war between them and Asgard, Orikal confirmed that Marnot had spoken the truth. Sensing that he would soon be attacked by Mangog, Orikal sought an audience with Ulik but Mangog arrived before Orikal could warn Ulik and quickly knocked out the Troll. Mangog then confronted Orikal, revealed that he had known that Orikal was guardian of futures but until that day had never suspected him to be the guardian of the Chalice of Ruins. Then, despite Orikal's protests, Mangog reached into his body and torn the chalice from his being. Mangog then gave the chalice to his master, Thanos. Later, after Thanos and Tarakis had taken the Map of All-Ending from Odin, the All-father went to Thor and reminded his son of how he had "long ago" whispered to him about the Chalice of Tears and the Map of All-Ending and who had possessed them. Odin then revealed that both items were now held by Mangog and Thanos. Orikal later showed Odin and Ulik a vision of a future in which Thanos used the two objects and the Illumination Stone to find and kidnap the Designate, and then killed Thor before her eyes, causing her to cry tears into the chalice from which he then drank and gained the power to unleash wave after wave of unimaginable death across the universe. When Odin asked Orikal if this future that he had revealed must come to pass, Orikal stated that nothing that existed could change it. However, seeing his son's defeat caused Odin to think of a way by which that catastrophe might be averted. Orikal later showed Odin that Thor was still trailing Thanos by a wide margin, and stated that Thanos and Mangog were close to the Designate so time was now growing short. When Thor, Firelord and a Recorder confronted Thanos, Mangog and Tarakis on a icy dead planet, Orikal showed Odin and Balder what was happening there and stated that events were passing just as they had viewed a fortnight earlier. Minutes later, Orikal was still showing Odin, Balder and Ulik what was happening as Mangog brutally beat Thor. Then, after Odin had infused the weapons created by Jagrfelm with the Odinforce, he commanded Orikal to open his dimension-piercing portal so that he could see Firelord and summon him to retrieve certain items that were crucial to victory. Orikal continued to show what was happening on the ice world as Firelord arrived, retrieved the weapons, and left to take them to Thor. Orikal also showed Thor's subsequent defeat of Thanos and how the villain died when he was consumed by the flames of Hell once Tarene caused her tears to fall upon him. Later, Orikal and Ulik were among the many across all planes of reality who received the news that Odin had died in battle with Surtur. Soon afterwards, when a grief-stricken Thor went to Orikal to ask if his father had somehow survived his battle with Surtur and still lived somewhere beyond their realm, Orikal stated that he had witnessed Odin's passing but searched anyway. Orikal then informed Thor that, after having scrutinized all realms and all planes of existence, he had seen no evidence that Odin still lived. When Thor reacted with anger, Orikal suggested that he should hurry to Midgard or else a mortal close to him would be lost as well. Once Thor had left, Geirrodur asked if the future that had been foretold might happen with Odin gone was as he feared
weaknesses: Orikal was vulnerable to a type of fire found in the Troll Kingdom.

Later, after Thanos and Tarakis had taken the Map of All-Ending from Odin, the All-father went to Thor and reminded his son of how he had "long ago" whispered to him about the Chalice of Tears and the Map of All-Ending and who had possessed them. Odin then revealed that both items were now held by Mangog and Thanos. Orikal later showed Odin and Ulik a vision of a future in which Thanos used the two objects and the Illumination Stone to find and kidnap the Designate, and then killed Thor before her eyes, causing her to cry tears into the chalice from which he then drank and gained the power to unleash wave after wave of unimaginable death across the universe. When Odin asked Orikal if this future that he had revealed must come to pass, Orikal stated that nothing that existed could change it. However, seeing his son's defeat caused Odin to think of a way by which that catastrophe might be averted. Orikal later showed Odin that Thor was still trailing Thanos by a wide margin, and stated that Thanos and Mangog were close to the Designate so time was now growing short. When Thor, Firelord and a Recorder confronted Thanos, Mangog and Tarakis on a icy dead planet, Orikal showed Odin and Balder what was happening there and stated that events were passing just as they had viewed a fortnight earlier. Minutes later, Orikal was still showing Odin, Balder and Ulik what was happening as Mangog brutally beat Thor. Then, after Odin had infused the weapons created by Jagrfelm with the Odinforce, he commanded Orikal to open his dimension-piercing portal so that he could see Firelord and summon him to retrieve certain items that were crucial to victory. Orikal continued to show what was happening on the ice world as Firelord arrived, retrieved the weapons, and left to take them to Thor. Orikal also showed Thor's subsequent defeat of Thanos and how the villain died when he was consumed by the flames of Hell once Tarene caused her tears to fall upon him. Later, Orikal and Ulik were among the many across all planes of reality who received the news that Odin had died in battle with Surtur. Soon afterwards, when a grief-stricken Thor went to Orikal to ask if his father had somehow survived his battle with Surtur and still lived somewhere beyond their realm, Orikal stated that he had witnessed Odin's passing but searched anyway. Orikal then informed Thor that, after having scrutinized all realms and all planes of existence, he had seen no evidence that Odin still lived. When Thor reacted with anger, Orikal suggested that he should hurry to Midgard or else a mortal close to him would be lost as well. Once Thor had left, Geirrodur asked if the future that had been foretold might happen with Odin gone was as he feared
weaknesses: Orikal was vulnerable to a type of fire found in the Troll Kingdom.
fields.notes: The idea that, as revealed in , Odin had "long ago" told Thor that Orikal possessed the Chalice of Ruins seems a bit inconsistent with the fact that nobody in Asgard had ever heard of Orikal before events in that took place in the modern age, fairly soon after Don Blake had first become Thor. It turned out that the unchangeable future that Orikal showed to Odin and Ulik in was not actually the future of the Earth-616 universe but that of an alternate timeline. However, it's unclear if Orikal was aware of this fact all along.

orlando kannor.name: Orlando Kannor
orlando kannor.origin: Orlando Kannor was ordered to steal some experimental computer chips, but he failed, mostly to the unexpected appearance of the Scarlet Spider. Orlando and his men ransacked Lady Octopus' lab and killed her men, but they were only able to recover a handful of the stolen chips. Kannor was knocked down by the Pro when he was sent by Lady Octopus to kill Mr. Tso. Kannor left Club Noir with the stolen inductor chips right before Aura, Override, and Looter attacked the place to retrieve them. Seeing him talking with Daily Bugle photographer Angela Yin, Kannor suspected Ben Reilly and did some research into his past, but couldn't find anything, thanks to Seward Trainer's cyber-intervention. Kannor then escorted Ben Reilly to the Daily Bugle Building. He later escorted Mr. Tso while he visited Alistaire Smythe's underground factory. As soon as he left Tso to look out for Ben Reilly, the Pro shot and killed Orlando's boss.

orlando sinclair.name: Orlando Sinclair
orlando sinclair.origin: Born to a black father and a Mexican mother, Orlando and his brother Mariano grew up in a world where they constantly missed out on opportunities because of their race. While Mariano joined a gang to give himself some identity, Orlando worked hard, playing football in high school, learning to act, sing, and dance. Passed over for a college scholarship, Orlando tried to find a job, with no luck. Turning to his talents, he was constantly tossed out of studios because he lacked the right connections. Meanwhile, Mariano was getting into trouble with a rival gang, and it was Orlando who paid the price. While waiting for a bus that would take him to yet another audition, the rival gang found Orlando and shot him in the back, leaving him paralyzed. Feeling guilty, his brother offered him an exoskeleton that would allow him to walk again (the suit itself was a modified version of the type of suit developed by Rampage), but in return, Orlando would have to kill members of the rival gang. Agreeing to the terms, Orlando donned the suit, but knew that killing the rival gang would serve no good, he fled. Eventually getting an acting job as Hit-Maker, "the superhero for the 90s." At a time when Wonder Man's powers were fueled by his rage, and he was constantly alienating people and studios, Hit-Maker was used as an example of a good superhero, the anti-Wonder Man. While facing Wonder Man in a fixed battle, Orlando was nearly killed by a bazooka blast from his brother's gang. While Wonder Man raced him to safety, the camera crew filming the event edited the footage to make it look like Wonder Man was responsible. Angered over this, Wonder Man confronted Hit-Maker in the hospital bed he had taken him to, demanding he stand up and face him. When Hit-Maker refused, Wonder Man hauled him to his feet, only for Hit-Maker (sans-armor) to collapse. As camera crews filmed this, Wonder Man fled, knowing how bad it would look if he continued the argument. As Hit-Maker eventually caught up to Wonder Man, the two finally agreed to join forces, and Hit-Maker explained his origin. The two, along with Beast, then assaulted Mariano's gang, but failed to capture Mariano when two of the Recession Raiders attacked. As the press arrived, Hit-Maker announced that he and Wonder Man were responsible, helping to boost Wonder Man's flagging image. ===After Civil War=== After the Civil War, he was listed as a potential recruit for the Initiative.
powers: Hit-Maker's suit gives him , speed, agility, endurance, reflexes, and durability.

orlean cooper.name: Orlean Cooper
orlean cooper.origin: Orlean Cooper was an exiled demon and New Orleans club owner that hired two New Orleans thieves, Gambit (Remy LeBeau) and 'Fast' Jack Jessup to steal a deck of cards from Morgan Penrose. The deck of cards was the Inficio Aquilus, a deck of tarot cards that would have empowered Orlean and would have allowed him to return from his exile. Orlean had never intended to pay either Gambit or 'Fast' Jack and played them off of one another until he was able to retrieve the cards from them. Gambit was later able to replace the cards in Orlean's possession with a pack of dummy cards. When Orlean attempted to perform the ritual to return from his exile with the dummy cards, he was scarred by the experience. He incorrectly assumed that 'Fast' Jack was the thief responsible for switching the decks and killed him in anger.

ororo munroe moira vii 1.name: Ororo Munroe (Moira-VII.1)
ororo munroe moira vii 1.origin: ===Sins of Sinister: First Decade=== Storm's origins and past equal those of her mainstream counterpart, in which she was an important political figure in the Quiet Council of Krakoa and the Great Ring of Arakko. The timeline diverged due to Mister Sinister's machinations of tainting humanity and mutandom by introducing his vile genome to uncountable victims through the Resurrection Protocols. By rejecting resurrection, Storm was free from his influence, but was also unaware that her closest allies had been corrupted versions of Sinister. One year later, the Quiet Council secretly lobotomized the consciousness of Krakoa and blamed Orchis for the attack, prompting Storm join the Avengers and the X-Men in striking at Orchis' forces together. Storm participated in the killing of Nimrod alongside with Thor. Over the following years, mutantkind machinated their control over the planet, eliminating opposition through treachery and deception. Their cruel ascension turned Storm disillusioned with her mission. Five years after Sinister had secretly infiltrated mutant society, Storm noticed that Nightcrawler had been replaced by an impostor, prompting Mister Sinister to reveal himself and his actions. The Quiet Council attempted to subdue Storm, but she escaped to Peru thanks to Lactuca, where she was met by Destiny and Mystique who proposed an alliance. left|150px Storm resisted in Arakko for the following years, leading her Brotherhood of Mutants against Mister Sinister's cloned Chimeras. However, a clone of Legion was used to obliterate Planet Arakko, and the few Arakkii survivors retread into hiding. Having lost much, Storm remained in the debris of Arakko, dubbed Asteroid S, with her right-hand man Jon Ironfire, former S.W.O.R.D. agents Cable and Wiz Kid and the Arakkii Khora of the Burning Heart and Quick as part of her Brotherhood. Mystique eventually approached Storm in Asteroid S to reveal about Mister Sinister's Moira Engine, a machine that could reset reality via clones of Moira. Storm and the Brotherhood went to Muir Island to retrieve Mister Sinister's lab, but Mystique betrayed them by impersonating Wiz Kid. She mortally wounded Storm, paralyzing her, and took the engine with her to the World Farm under Orbis Stellaris' guidance. ===Year 100=== Over the course of a century, Storm led the underground freedom fighters known as the Brotherhood to fight against both Sinister's Red Diamond Empire and Stellaris' Interstellar Compact. Storm became known as "the Old Witch." A rival insurgent cell called the Freedom Force trasmitted the location and schematics of the Compact's Death Sphere to Arakko Base. After Mystique's death, Destiny joined with Storm and the Brotherhood to set off the Moira Engine and reset the timeline. They attacked the Death Sphere, but before they destroyed the Center-Sun that contained the Moiras, Storm had Destiny killed. Storm believed that Arrako's destruction did not justify eliminating an entire timeline so her true plan was to teleport the Moiras away to defuse and guard. Khora magnified Storm's mutant powers and she mixed it with magic to open a wormhole that teleported the World Farm away. However, the price of this feat was her life and she died smiling. ===Year 1000=== Over the next 900 years, Storm's brotherhood, now led by Jon Ironfire, turned the World Farm into an impregnable fortress. After 900 years of searching, Mr. Sinister finally found the World Farm and his lab. Pursued by an Empire of the Red Diamond armada, Sinister and Ironfire entered into a temporary alliance. Sinister used genetic material of Storm and Hope Summers, together with five Brotherhood mutants, to resurrect Storm, though without the memories of the original. Boosted by Khora, Storm destroyed the armada. Lacking the experience of her original self, Storm did not shield herself from the resultant radiation, and died once again.

fields.history: ===Sins of Sinister: First Decade=== Storm's origins and past equal those of her mainstream counterpart, in which she was an important political figure in the Quiet Council of Krakoa and the Great Ring of Arakko. The timeline diverged due to Mister Sinister's machinations of tainting humanity and mutandom by introducing his vile genome to uncountable victims through the Resurrection Protocols. By rejecting resurrection, Storm was free from his influence, but was also unaware that her closest allies had been corrupted versions of Sinister. One year later, the Quiet Council secretly lobotomized the consciousness of Krakoa and blamed Orchis for the attack, prompting Storm join the Avengers and the X-Men in striking at Orchis' forces together. Storm participated in the killing of Nimrod alongside with Thor. Over the following years, mutantkind machinated their control over the planet, eliminating opposition through treachery and deception. Their cruel ascension turned Storm disillusioned with her mission. Five years after Sinister had secretly infiltrated mutant society, Storm noticed that Nightcrawler had been replaced by an impostor, prompting Mister Sinister to reveal himself and his actions. The Quiet Council attempted to subdue Storm, but she escaped to Peru thanks to Lactuca, where she was met by Destiny and Mystique who proposed an alliance. left|150px Storm resisted in Arakko for the following years, leading her Brotherhood of Mutants against Mister Sinister's cloned Chimeras. However, a clone of Legion was used to obliterate Planet Arakko, and the few Arakkii survivors retread into hiding. Having lost much, Storm remained in the debris of Arakko, dubbed Asteroid S, with her right-hand man Jon Ironfire, former S.W.O.R.D. agents Cable and Wiz Kid and the Arakkii Khora of the Burning Heart and Quick as part of her Brotherhood. Mystique eventually approached Storm in Asteroid S to reveal about Mister Sinister's Moira Engine, a machine that could reset reality via clones of Moira. Storm and the Brotherhood went to Muir Island to retrieve Mister Sinister's lab, but Mystique betrayed them by impersonating Wiz Kid. She mortally wounded Storm, paralyzing her, and took the engine with her to the World Farm under Orbis Stellaris' guidance. ===Year 100=== Over the course of a century, Storm led the underground freedom fighters known as the Brotherhood to fight against both Sinister's Red Diamond Empire and Stellaris' Interstellar Compact. Storm became known as "the Old Witch." A rival insurgent cell called the Freedom Force trasmitted the location and schematics of the Compact's Death Sphere to Arakko Base. After Mystique's death, Destiny joined with Storm and the Brotherhood to set off the Moira Engine and reset the timeline. They attacked the Death Sphere, but before they destroyed the Center-Sun that contained the Moiras, Storm had Destiny killed. Storm believed that Arrako's destruction did not justify eliminating an entire timeline so her true plan was to teleport the Moiras away to defuse and guard. Khora magnified Storm's mutant powers and she mixed it with magic to open a wormhole that teleported the World Farm away. However, the price of this feat was her life and she died smiling. ===Year 1000=== Over the next 900 years, Storm's brotherhood, now led by Jon Ironfire, turned the World Farm into an impregnable fortress. After 900 years of searching, Mr. Sinister finally found the World Farm and his lab. Pursued by an Empire of the Red Diamond armada, Sinister and Ironfire entered into a temporary alliance. Sinister used genetic material of Storm and Hope Summers, together with five Brotherhood mutants, to resurrect Storm, though without the memories of the original. Boosted by Khora, Storm destroyed the armada. Lacking the experience of her original self, Storm did not shield herself from the resultant radiation, and died once again.
abilities: Storm has the same abilities as her Earth-616 counterpart.
fields.trivia: Al Ewing originally wrote the wormhole scene as just mutant power but decided to add magic following Storm's magic ancestry being revisted in .

orphelus.name: Orphelus
orphelus.origin: Orphelus was a Roman magician born in Italy. During the third century, he was a legionary, and found a magical pool of blood in Britain. Drinking the blood gave him a greatly extended life, but after seventeen hundred years, he came to see his immortality as a sin. In the modern era, Orphelus lured Dracula to the pool, believing both of them needed to die. He used a magical amulet to destroy the blood pool and died as it boiled away. Dracula was also badly injured, but his vampiric powers allowed him to survive.
powers: Orphelus was effectively immortal, as long as he drank from the magical blood pool he discovered.

orrek.name: Orrek
orrek.origin: In 6,000 BC, which was about 12,000 years after Atlantis sank beneath the ocean, Prince Orrek of the nomadic Homo mermani Eastern Sea tribe arrived at the ruins of Atlantis. He travelled with his brother King Stegor who led the army to battle the army of the Western Sea led by King Tanas. The warring nations both bid to conquer the city and its hidden treasures. King Stegor died in the battle by the Queen Elanna of the Western Sea. Orrek, then sent Prince Kamuu on patrol, with the plan that the prince would be killed, so he could attain the throne of the tribe.

orrible oress.name: Orrible Oress
orrible oress.origin: Orrible Oress was a mobster who operated out of the town of Middleton in the 1940's. Developing a special kind of exploding light bulb, Oress had his men plant them all over the city, leaving city officials stumped where the the explosive bulbs could be placed. This forced the mayor to order a mandatory blackout of the city. This played into Oress' plan as he sent send his minions out to commit a large scale robbery. This was witnessed by police officer Pat Murphy who donned his guise of the homeless super-hero known as the Vagabond. The hero followed Orrible's gang back to his windmill hide out. There, the hero defeated Oress' gang, and in a one-on-one battle, the Vagabond proved the superior opponent, even though Orrible was armed with a gun and a knife. In the end, Oress was thrown from the top of the windmill to his death. His gang was apprehended shortly thereafter.
weapons: Oress was armed with a pistol and a knife. He planted explosive light bulbs that would go off when someone connected an electrical current to them. The explosives were highly destructive and lethal to those in close range.

fields.unusual_features: Orrible has a massive mole on the bridge of his nose.

orson kasloff.name: Orson Kasloff
orson kasloff.origin: Professor Orson Kasloff was a brilliant scientist chemist, considered by some the foremost analytical chemist in the world, who felt that he didn't earn enough money for his scientific work and turned to crime. When his first attempt at a break-in failed because he hadn't considered burglar alarms, he decided to search out other criminals to partner up with. Failing to make contact with the underworld, he saw the Human Torch in action and decided to defeat the young hero in order to impress the underworld. He bought an old castle and built an armored suit made out of asbestos. He was defeated and turned over to the police by the Human Torch. Lacking villainous plans, he hoped to avenge himself from the Torch, but Storm died before he could. Kasloff tried to start back his criminal career, as he was annoyed that people would forget him with Johnny Storm dead. He tried to rob a fast food restaurant, now carrying around an air canister due to having survived cancer, probably due to the suit itself, but was annoyed to find the cashier was afraid of him because he was wearing asbestos and feared for her health. Asbestos Man ran into the Great Lakes Avengers who were on the run from a fear influenced mob themselves. They all assumed fighting stances surrounding Orson, but since Orson wasn't willing to fight and no one in the team was willing to even touch a man wearing an asbestos suit they all ended up staying that way for hours until they all gave up. Orson confided in them his fears of no one remembering him and being an awful super villain. Mr. Immortal was able to get him to surrender quietly with the promise that they would remember him as one of their villains (though they refused his toxic mask as a trophy). He was then removed by an ambulance and hazmat-suited staff. He was later stated by Johnny Storm to have died, presumably from his condition. However he, or someone wearing his costume, was in prison with Ziggy Pig and Silly Seal.
weaknesses: Due to his exposure to the carcinogenic asbestos, Kasloff contracted a cancer deeply affecting him.

orson whales.name: Orson Whales
orson whales.first_appearance: Peter Porker, The Spectacular Spider-Ham Vol 1 9
orson whales.origin: Orson Whales was an anthropomorphic whale who had succeeded as a radio star, staging a mock invasion of aliens from Mars, and later as a film director. Whales' friend J. Jonah Jackal believed that Whales had been the best film director, but Hollywood sharks (who were likely literal sharks) kicked him away from their city. As an elderly whale, Whales lived in a suburban environment in rural New Jersey, taking meager pleasure in eating (not meagerly eating, mind you). Whales was still famous to some extent, partly due to his immense physical size - a Japanese joke suggested that Whales and giant monster Hog-zilla could almost share shirt size (although Hog-zilla did not wear a shirt). Whales then had a "close encounter of the third kind" when an alien from outer space (later called B.O.) knocked at his door. Because of his previous martial invasion radio show, Whales was unable to convince his neighbors of the existence of this alien. Whales then decided to sent the alien, by post, to his friend Jackal with a note so that Jackal, by then a reputed newspaper editor, could inform the world about the real nature of the alien. However, Jackal was unable to grab hold of the alien, who returned to outer space; Jackal decided not to report about B.O. without proof.

ort beast.name: Ort-Beast
ort beast.origin: The Ort-Beast is an extradimensional alien. It inhabits a pocket universe which is either within the Shadow Cloak of Devil-Slayer, or accessed through the Cloak. Its world is ever-changing, but the creature considers it the best of all possible worlds. It is unclear whether the Ort-Beast has experiences with other worlds. The Ort-Beast has been described by Devil-Slayer as one of the crystalline inhabitants of its world. Whether there are actually others like it is unconfirmed. None has been depicted. The creature has been described as both sentient and highly intelligent, but apparently can not properly speak. Its only vocalization is repeating the word "Ort", from which its name derives. It has red skin, claws in its hands, and a beak in its face. At some point, the Ort-Beast encountered and fought the Hulk, who was briefly trapped in its world. The Hulk believed that the creature was trying to eat him, but its motivation is somewhat unclear. The Ort-Beast viewed him as a "soft green being", and the narration describes the Hulk as the creature's odd playmate. Due to the realm around them which is constantly changing, the two combatants could not get the upper hand in this combat. The Ort-Beast's claws were prevented from harming the Hulk, while the Beast teleported away from his fists when he attacked. The Hulk was unhappy with this ever-changing world which prevented him from smashing monsters. He threatened to smash the world itself. The Ort-Beast reappeared behind the Hulk's back, but it was quite puzzled by his words. It wondered why the Hulk was dissatisfied with the world. Devil-Slayer and Valkyrie interrupted the fight, by offering the Hulk a chance to return to Earth. The Hulk attacked Devil-Slayer, who was the one who trapped him in the first place. The Ort-Beast briefly attempted to follow the Hulk. When the Hulk disappeared (teleported away by Devil-Slayer), the creature was left alone in its world again. At a later point, Hellcat was practicing with her own version of the Shadow Cloak, and was also trying to entertain the Hulk. She tried pulling something out of the teleportation cloak, and accidentally pulled out the head of the Ort-Beast. Hulk went into attack mode and assaulted the Shadow Cloak, accidentally hurting Hellcat in the process. During the attack, the Ort-Beast disappeared. Probably having returned to its own world.
abilities: The creature apparently understands words in the English language, even if he can not speak it himself/itself.
weaknesses: The creature cannot speak any coherent language, and just keeps repeating "Ort". This limits its ability to communicate with others.

ortlinda.name: Ortlinda
ortlinda.origin: When Hela had taken over Valhalla and turned it into a reflection of her own realm, Niffleheim, Odin sent Ortlinda and the rest of the Valkyrior ahead of him to fight off Hela, but she and her sisters were slain by Hela's minions. When Odin got there, he plead with Hela to bring them back to life and stop her madness, but she explained that after a recent encounter with Thor and Lady Sif, she realized that she had wanted to express her own feelings of compassion and desire to be a woman, but could not since she was burdened with being the goddess of death. Odin then took pity on Hela and granted her the wisdom and knowledge she sought. She went back to Niffleheilm, allowing Valhalla to return to its original form, resurrecting Ortlinda and the rest of the Valkyries in the process.

Thor, on his way to find his half-brother (as Hoder had prophetized Vidar's role in the coming conflict) detected them, and stealthily spied upon them, learning their goals and that Ymir had joined them, tanks to a Storm Giant Orvarg beat up as he kept speaking those vital information out loud. Thor then attacked them, and with the timely arrival of Vidar, Orvarg's crew was defeated, but he escaped, capturing Grid in the process, taking her hostage and threatening to kill her if Vidar didn't surrendered to him. He then delivered her to the Giants leaders Grim Graybeard and Bjorn the White, who intended respectively intended to use her as a gift to Odin or as a bait for Vidar.

The Kid accepted the challenge but as the fight was set to begin some of the townsfolk realized that Orville Jones was the notorious hypnotist that hypnotized his opponents into losing during shootouts. orwell taylor.name: Orwell Taylor
orwell taylor.origin: Orwell Taylor was once a General in the United States Army. Orwell and his wife had two sons, Maxwell and Hugh Taylor. As an adult, Hugh joined the Army where he became friends with Samuel Caulkin and after he left the Army he got a job working at the superhuman prison known as the Vault where he became close friends with Curtis Elkins. Hugh was smothered to death by Venom. Orwell, mad with grief, wanted to find a way to avenge the death of his son. Orwell gathered together several of his son Hugh's former army buddies and fellow guardsmen at the vault and outfitted them with armor based on the armor the Guardsman wore (which was based on designs stolen from Iron Man. Maxwell become "Screech", Samuel Caulkin become "Ramshot", and Curtis Elkins become "Sentry". He named this group the Jury and made it their mission to bring Venom to justice. Orwell and the Jury failed in their first outing against Venom. Later they kidnapped and drugged Spider-Man and tricked him into helping them steal a government transporter ray that they planned to modify to kill Venom. Again they met with failure. Orwell and the Jury later began to get away from their original goals and began working with the Life Foundation. Orwell was eventually apprehended by the authorities for his illegal dealings with the Life Foundation.

osamu moroboshi.name: Osamu Moroboshi
osamu moroboshi.origin: Osamu Moroboshi was the CEO of Moroboshi International, a competitor of Stark International. At some unspecified point in time, he came into contact with Controller, who implanted him with a more advanced, undetectable version of his slave discs. Still recovering from the grievous injuries he suffered during the Armor Wars, Controller used Moroboshi as a proxy in an elaborate plan to take control of Stark International and use its resources to heal his broken body. Moroboshi contacted Justin Hammer and several representatives from HYDRA, the Hand, and Roxxon Energy representing a mysterious "patron." After Tony Stark was believed to have died from neurocellular degradation, Moroboshi enacted a plan to place Morgan Stark as the figurehead CEO, under the reasoning that Morgan was Tony's next of kin. This plan was complicated by the fact that Tony had willed the company to James Rhodes, so Morgan attempted to remove Rhodes by planting evidence that framed Rhodes for Tony's murder. This plan quickly fell apart when Tony was revealed to be alive, and Moroboshi began to saw Morgan as a liability that could implicate him. Moroboshi attempted to cover his tracks by deploying battle droids to assassinate Rhodes, but this plot failed when Rhodes, in his War Machine armor, and Iron Man's Telepresence Armor defeated the robot stormtroopers in a standing battle. With Morgan implicated in the conspiracy and attempting to flee the country, Moroboshi has Berserker-7 shoot the tires out of his car, sending him careening off a cliff. Moroboshi calls his patron, telling him there is now nothing that can be traced back to them. But Moroboshi's own usefulness had also come to an end. Controller activated a kill switch in Moroboshi's slave disc, killing him and making it look like he died of a stroke.

oscar stamp.origin: In the year 1859, Oscar Stamp was part of a group of Marauders, who kidnapped freaks, fools, and all types of misshapen folk off the streets of London and took them underground. Dr. Nathaniel Essex hired the thugs to continue their work, so he could perform experiments on the victims in the name of science. One of them was a boy, named Danny Edge, who had stopped talking after witnessing the murder of his parents. After awakening, the immortal mutant, En Sabah Nur, Nur ordered the Marauders to take him to Dr. Essex; meanwhile, the time-travelers, Cyclops and Phoenix, arrived. Cyclops and Phoenix thwarted Nur and Mister Sinister's plan to conquer the United Kingdom and Oscar and Daniel journeyed to America to start a new life. At the immigration office, they claimed to be father and son, by the name of Summers, inspired by the married couple that had saved them from their fates.

oshemar.name: Oshemar
oshemar.origin: An inventor from an alien dimension known as the Caldaran Dominions, Oshemar's people fought a long war against the Sextus Hive, losing much in the war. As the Sextus Hive had protection against most conventional weaponry, Oshemar saw need to produce a new, unconventional weapon. Constructing the Unbinding Stone, Oshemar invented a weapon capable of repealing the very laws of physics. Wielding the stone in a final assault on the Hive's queenworld, Oshemar found every boundary in his path, including time itself, destroyed. With the battle won, Oshemar realized too late that the Unbinding Stone could not be stopped, leading to the death of the entire Sextus Hive, then the Caldarans, and everything else in his dominion, with the exception of Oshemar himself, who created a dimensional rift to escape. Unconsciously carrying the stone with him across worlds, he found himself in Asgard, where the stone was somehow rendered inert in the crossing. With his final words, he swore he would find a means to destroy the stone, but died before he could do so.

oskar kessler.name: Oskar Kessler
oskar kessler.origin: Captain Kessler was a member of the Nazis who was active during World War II. He was a brilliant inventor who came up with designs for massive robots that could be piloted by soldiers. It was not until March of 1943 that one of his superiors took his plans seriously. ossawa.name: Ossawa
ossawa.origin: Ossawa was an abnormally large condor that lived during the days of the American Frontier. The massive bird hunted the plains where the Comanche tribe led by Grey Eagle also hunted, threatening the food supply of the tribe. When Red Warrior discovered the bird, he determined that it must die so that his tribe could still hunt for food. Climbing up to the birds next, Reed Warrior had found that Ossawa had laid three eggs and smashed them all. Ossawa then attacked Red Warrior, who fought the condor off with his knife. The massive bird of prey returned for another attack but was struck in the heart by one of Red Warrior's arrows and fell to her death. Red Warrior took one of Ossawa's feathers as a trophy of his victory.

ossem.name: Ossem
ossem.origin: Ossem was one of the great patriarchs of the Atlanteans 2000 years ago. Most of Ossem's sons were slaughtered by Atlantean barbarians. Ossem's son Balaal began recruiting followers for the ancient god Set and denounced the Atlantean's god Neptune demanding revenge against the barbarians who killed his brothers while Ossem preached pacifism. When Ossem asked Neptune to intercede, he was originally rebuffed and was told that Neptune did not perform parlor tricks for the weak of faith. Ossem was later captured by Balaal's cult of Set followers who had created a proto-Serpent Crown called the Golden Serpent powered by their psychic energy in the hopes of returning Set to Earth. When the cult tried to sacrifice Ossem, Neptune rained down destruction killing everyone in the cult, but spared Ossem. The Atlantean people at this point scattered and Ossem spent the rest of his life reuniting his people. On his deathbed, Neptune promised Ossem from that point forward he would take a more active role in protecting the Atlanteans. The period where Neptune nurtured the Atlanteans people and dwelt amongst them is seen as a golden age in Atlantean history.
powers: Atlantean Physiology

oswald boeglin.name: Oswald Boeglin
oswald boeglin.origin: Not much was known of the mutant known as Bulwark before he was found and recruited by Emplate. This powerhouse joined a team that Emplate gathered to torment Generation X, including Murmur, Vincente, and DOA. Before the young teens returned to the Massachusetts Academy from their outing into the city, they were attacked by Emplate's Hellions. Skin, who had separated from the group to drop off Synch at his parents' house was ambushed by Bulwark and brought back to the Institute. The Hellions were successful in capturing the young mutants, but M had telepathically called for help and it was answered by the X-Man Bishop. M took out her frustrations on Bulwark, punching him through the school's Bio-Sphere and then flying after him. As he was about to attack M, his muscles suddenly withered away. Knowing that he was defeated, he fled along with Vincente. Leech—then a ward of Generation X and resident of the Bio-dome—was the one responsible for the atrophy of Bulwark's powers, and M thanked him for his help. With Penance's realignment of alliances Generation X was successful in stopping the team. Bulwark did not have a happy ending. Sometime later he was captured by operatives of the revamped Weapon X program. Along with many other mutants, he was rounded up and put into a concentration camp called Neverland and was subsequently killed in the gas chambers.

other alien entity.name: Other (Alien Entity)
other alien entity.species: Cosmic Being; Alien; Extinction Weapon ("cursed idea woven with Mortoturgy")
other alien entity.origin: The being known only as the Other is an extra-dimensional being that manifests in our reality as a race of diminutive grey-skinned humanoids. Although they appear as an entire species, they are in fact just projections of the same mind and have no real existence independent of it. For countless millennia, it has been engaged in a war with the cosmic being known as the Scrier for control of the multiverse. According to the Vishanti, the Other is in truth one of the Extinction King's lost Extinction Weapons called Deathblood, a war-machine of their own making, because it was forged in their ancient struggle against it, and the force responsible for the Great Cataclysm that sank Atlantis. In shame, the Vishanti later claimed to be Agatha Harkness' saviors, when in reality they were merely attempting to clean up a catastrophe born of their own long-standing failure. In 1947, the Other visited the planet Zenn-La, and destroyed every living being and structure on the planet, killing Shalla-Bal alongside countless others. Their presence was enough to render Galactus and the Silver Surfer comatose and unable to interfere. Several years later, the Other would abduct several humans from Earth, including comics writer Stan Lee and widow Henrietta Rose. Finding Lee unsuitable for their purposes, they soon returned him to his office with his memory erased, but subjected Rose to various painful experiments. She would be rescued by the Silver Surfer, despite the Other's attempts to destroy him. In the modern age, the Other would once again return to Earth, tormenting Henrietta Rose and her daughter. The Silver Surfer once again confronted it, driving its influence from Rose's mind, but was overwhelmed by swarms of the Other's creatures when he attempted to pursue it back to its own dimension. The Other infected him, attempting to erase him from the memories of every being in existence. In attempting to cure him, Agatha Harkness briefly made mental contact with the Other and was almost destroyed herself. Eventually, working alongside Scrier, the Silver Surfer was able to barricade shut the portal between dimensions, trapping the Other within. When Asgard was displaced to Earth, this disrupted the barricade sufficiently that the Other was once again able to manifest beyond its own dimension. Scrier attempted to manipulate Thor into sacrificing himself to placate the Other, but the agreement was interrupted by Galactus, who threatened to attack both players in this ancient conflict. Fearing the destruction that would ensure from such a conflict, the Other agreed to a half-billion year truce with Scrier.

other spider totem.name: Other (Spider-Totem)
other spider totem.origin: ===Origin=== The Spider-Man of Earth-616 was chosen by the Great Weaver to be the receptacle of the Other when he became Spider-Man. However, Spider-Man subconsciously rejected and suppressed the spider side of himself until he encountered the Inheritor Morlun, who fed on the essence of totemic avatars. After vanquishing Morlun and becoming aware of his totemic abilities for the first time, Peter Parker began to weaken - discovering he was dying of an unknown mystical affliction - and concurrently had prophetic visions of his death at the hands of the Morlun, who had returned from death. When Morlun finally made his move and mortally wounded Peter, the Other took over Peter's body and killed the Inheritor. After Peter seemingly died from his injuries, the Other transported his body to the Brooklyn Bridge and spun a cocoon. The Other confronted Peter's psyche within his mindscape, claiming to be the manifestation of his totemic spider-powers and telling him that his human side had died, but that he could return to life if he embraced his spider side. Peter reluctantly agreed, and emerged from the cocoon completely healed of his prior wounds and with enhanced powers - thereby "conquering" death. 150px|left|thumb|As the Great Weaver (Multiverse)|Great Weaver Shortly after Peter's resurrection, the Other manifested as a swarm of pirate spiders and attacked Stark Tower to eat Peter's old shed skin, cocooning the top of Stark Tower in webbing. When he arrived, Spider-Man discovered that the spiders had used his shed skin to form a humanoid body similar to the Gatekeeper, albeit being distinctly female in shape. Spider-Man attempted to fight her using his augmented powers, but the Other's manifestation retreated, easily ripping through a vibranium-reinforced wall. Declaring herself to be Spider-Man's "Other," the entity explained to Peter that Morlun should have killed him, but the Great Weaver had resurrected him. The female entity stated that another spider-totem had opposed this and sent her to kill Peter and restore the natural order. Calling herself "Ero" after the genus of spider comprising her body, the female creature claimed she was Peter's opposite, his nemesis and his significant other; warning him to "evolve or die" before escaping down a drain. 150px|right|thumb|As Ero Ero retreated to an old church across the street from Stark Tower, where she spun a cocoon and took on a human form that was the opposite of Peter in every way: female to his male, dark-skinned to his light, and blonde to his brown hair. Sometime later, Spider-Man met up with Beast at the old church, where they discovered Ero's empty cocoon. ===Civil War=== Having taken on human form, Ero assumed the name "Miss Arrow" and became the school nurse at Midtown High School to monitor and test Peter. When Midtown High was attacked by three Mysterios, Miss Arrow found herself in contact with Quentin Beck. Beck implied that she was more than an innocent bystander, mentioning that he knew about Miss Arrow's "superiors," and that he could easily see through her charade. He told her that she must work to keep Peter at the school because his superiors wanted it, and so did hers; though Arrow claimed to not know what he was talking about. Beck vanished, although Arrow later found herself face-to-face with Francis Klum. Klum attempted to take her hostage, telling that she was to become a pawn in a much larger game. Angered, Arrow revealed her true nature to him by extending large stingers from her wrists. Telling Klum she was no one's pawn, she plunged one of them into his chest. Before she could finish him off, he teleported. 150px|left|thumb|As Miss Arrow Arrow later convinced Spider-Man to stay at the school, a task which was complicated when Peter became a fugitive for going against the Registration Act, as he had to use an Image Inducer to disguise himself as "Ben Reilly" to continue his career at the school. When Debra Whitman got into an altercation with Flash Thompson, Arrow moved to attack her with her stingers but was distracted when Betty Brant remarked that she and Flash used to date. Despite being tempted to attack Betty as well, Arrow shook her hand instead, making the veiled threat to eat her. Flash and Betty Brant went on a date, which clashed with Arrow's plans for Flash. When Betty had to use the restroom, Ero emerged from the toilet as thousands of spiders, frightening Betty. When Flash and the restaurant manager came to the scene after Betty had left the bathroom, only some cocaine and straw were found, making the manager think Betty had used the cocaine. Later at Midtown High, Peter Parker was talking to Flash when Arrow walked into the room. Peter barely activated the image inducer in time to conceal his true face from her. Peter found it strange that his spider-sense hadn't warned him of Arrow's approach, since in the past it had always warned him when there was a risk of somebody seeing him and learning his secret identity. Ar
abilities: When manifested as Ero/Miss Arrow, it could into a swarm of spiders and control them. It also acquired sufficient medical knowledge to act as a nurse.

fields.notes: portrays Miss Arrow in . Due to the events of Mephisto rewriting history, the powers Peter developed during The Other (and the powers obtained from his incident with the Queen) have mysteriously disappeared. The manifestation of the entity known as Miss Arrow would never exist outside of The Other story arc, though the Other appeared in its "Ero" and giant spider forms in the Scarlet Spider series. Ero was introduced as an antagonistic spider totem opposed to the Great Weaver, who had resurrected Peter Parker, and manifested to kill him and restore the natural order. However, a retcon implemented during combined Ero with aspects of the Great Weaver into "The Other", an entity whose nature has been expanded upon in Spider-Verse. The remaining aspects of the Great Weaver, such as weaving the Web of Life, were given to the Master Weaver. According to Uatu, the Other is the manifestation of Peter's spider abilities and a representative of the Great Weaver. This was retconned in and Spider-Verse, which established the Other as an entity independent of Spider-Man - who possesses powers regardless of whether he is its vessel or not. According to Old Man Spider, The Other, The Bride and The Scion are unique totemic entities in the Multiverse. The retcon that the Other was the spider-totem who resurrected Peter leaves its reasons for manifesting as Ero and trying to kill Peter unclear. According to the , the Other is unique to Earth-616, though this is proven false by it resurrecting the Peter Parker of Earth-982 and has attempted to claim the Peter Parker of Earth-70134 as its avatar.
fields.trivia: Ero is similar in appearance to the Gatekeeper, and at one point appears as the Gatekeeper, though whether they were meant to be related or one-in-the-same is unknown. Its appearance in was based on Spider-Man's costume. The Other has been described as the personification of Spider-Man's spider-powers - and by extension those of his clone Kaine; but despite this it has been rejected by and separated from them and even killed without the total loss of their spider-powers. Despite having repeatedly faced life-threatening danger and often been enraged, the Spider-Man of Earth-616 never transformed into a spider-humanoid monster. During his fight with Spider-Man, Ero stated that the wrist stingers could only be used against threats of supernatural origin. This proved to be false, as Kaine was able to use them whenever they wanted. Although he had been transformed into the Other's form, the Peter Parker of Earth-982 appeared to have been able to retain his human mindset even during the transformation.

otis johnson ii.origin: ===Early Life=== Otis Danger Johnson was accidentally exposed to a chemical at an A.I.M. facility, making him indestructible and impervious to pain. ===Nightwing Restorations=== Johnson worked as an administrative assistant for the Nightwing Restorations Ltd. and due to the working style of this company he normally helped Colleen Wing and Misty Knight on many cases. He tried to act a tough thug which was very unconvincing. He was attacked by the Atlantean, Orka, who was looking for Misty and Colleen. Being away from the sea caused oxygen imbalance in his brain. Because he could not answer his questions he pummeled Otis around the office. He could not understand why he wouldn't die. After a while stopped hitting Otis and waited patiently for them to return. After that the two became friends. During an investigation of Celia Ricadonna, after the murders of some of their clients, he posed as a parking attendant at an auction she was having to sell a microchip that could destroy the global economy. He later stalled the bodyguards long enough to stop Ricadonna from escaping.. ===Heroes for Hire=== During the Civil War, Misty and Coleen were contacted by Iron Man to reform Heroes for Hire in order to track down superhumans refusing to comply with the Superhuman Registration Act. Initially hesitant, the pair eventually created a team including Shang-Chi, Humbug, Orka, Black Cat, Paladin, and a new Tarantula. Otis was kept on for administration. When Ricadonna planned a prison break, she sent a bomb to their office, destroying it with only Otis inside. Though he was fine, he was concerned about losing his job. He tried to act a tough thug which was very unconvincing. He was attacked by the Atlantean, Orka, who was looking for Misty and Colleen. Being away from the sea caused oxygen imbalance in his brain. Because he could not answer his questions he pummeled Otis around the office. He could not understand why he wouldn't die. After a while stopped hitting Otis and waited patiently for them to return. He later stalled the bodyguards long enough to stop Ricadonna from escaping.. ===Heroes for Hire=== During the Civil War, Misty and Coleen were contacted by Iron Man to reform Heroes for Hire in order to track down superhumans refusing to comply with the Superhuman Registration Act. When Ricadonna planned a prison break, she sent a bomb to their office, destroying it with only Otis inside. Though he was fine, he was concerned about losing his job. otr hriedmarson.name: Otr Hriedmarson
otr hriedmarson.species: Son of a Vanir and of a witch of Svartalfheim (see notes)
otr hriedmarson.origin: Otr was the third son of Hriedmar of the Vanir and of a witch of Svartalfheim. Thus, he was gifted at birth with the talent of a changer of shapes. He lived in the Inn of Hriedmar along with his two older brothers Regin and Fafnir. One day, when he had been sent by Hriedmar as a human-sized otter to catch a supper, he encountered the young prince Odin Borson and the time-travelling Loki. While Odin was astonished by the creature greeting them, Loki quickly killed it. His meat was eaten, and from his fur were made two cloaks. When Loki and Odin came to the Inn and listened to Hriedmar talking about his third son, Odin quickly understood that they had killed Otr. Just as soon, Fafnir and Regin entered in arms, recognizing Otr's fur on the two travellers' backs. The feud was settled by Loki who brought a blood price for Otr's death, gold stolen from Andvari the Dwarf, who had cursed it. While Loki and Odin were left alone, Fafnir, compelled by the curse, killed Hriedmar, left Regin for dead and stole all of the gold for himself. Regin then buried Otr and Hriedmar, and swore revenge upon Fafnir and all Asgardians.
powers: Due to the magical legacy from his mother's side, Otr was granted at birth the ability of changing shapes, among the river-beast such as an otter. However, he kept human size in this form.

family: Hriedmar (father, deceased) "Ma" (unnamed witch of Svartalfheim, possibly deceased)

ott.name: Ott
ott.origin: By his own accounts, Captain Ott is a Martian who was sent to Earth by the leader the "Great One" to obtain a Super T.N.T. formula created by Mr. Carson of the Carson Explosive Company, so that they could defend Mars from an attack by another unidentified alien race. To this end, the Great One ordered Ott and his companions to work with Clifton Ritton, giving them orders to follow him as they would the Great One. Mr. Ritton only agreed to help if they invade planet Earth and make him emperor of the United States. Feeling they had no choice, the Martians agreed to these terms. Tracking Carson down, they blasted the tracks ahead of the train he was riding in causing it to crash. When Ott and his partner demanded the formula from Carson (who's spine was broken in the crash) he refused to hand it over. The Martians were in for a surprise when the android Human Torch (also a passenger on the train) attacked and sent them fleeing. Later, after the Torch handed the formula over to Carson's daughter Diane, he was going out to test the new explosive in a safe environment. He was ambushed by the Martians and captured. Placed in an electric chair, the Torch was helpless to stop Ott and his comrade to capture Diane and tie her to railroad tracks in a bid for Ritton to scare her into giving out the formula. Ritton explained to all gathered his motivation in this plot, however the Torch managed to free himself and Diane and sent Ritton fleeing. As the Torch went off to apprehend Ritton, Diane learned the plight of the Martians but wasn't able to bring herself to turn over the formula. However, when the Torch returned the two realized how desperately the Martians needed the explosives and feeling it wasn't safe on Earth turned it over to the Martians.
weapons: He used a dagger to threaten Mr. Carson.

otto briefer.name: Otto Briefer
otto briefer.origin: The Mad Mechanic was a Nazi scientist who was active during World War II. Located in the Swiss Alps, he created a number of high tech gadgets to help the Nazi war effort. By 1944, he had made his presence known by sending Swiss watches rigged with explosives to the United States. These watches were to be used by the Navy. However, when one went off killing a commanding officer, it was witnessed by the Young Allies who then disposed of the other watches. Finding a message from the Mad Mechanic in one of the pieces of shrapnel, the Young Allies tracked the Mad Mechanic to his hideout in the Alps. Despite his efforts to kill the Young Allies, the young heroes made their way into his hideout but were snared in his wire gun. He then left the Allies while he used his massive spiked ball tank to destroy Allied defenses. When the Young Allies freed themselves, Bucky and Knuckles O'Toole went after him, sending his tank off a cliff and taking the Mad Mechanic prisoner. The Mad Mechanic turned the tide, knocking the two youths out, retaking his base, and attacking the other Young Allies with his army of robots. As the Young Allies fought off these mechanical attackers, the Mad Mechanic led another army of robots to attack the Allied Forces. The Allies soon caught up with him and easily forced his command microphone from his hands. When Bucky ordered the robots to attack each other, the Mad Mechanic attempted to stop his creations from fighting and was trampled to death.
weapons: The Mad Mechanic had access to cannons, explosives and other firearms. He protected himself with a gun that fire coiled wire to ensnare his foes.

otto frick.name: Otto Frick
otto frick.origin: Otto Frick was a Nazi colonel in charge of a group, consisting of his Nazi soldiers. He killed the wife of a nomad leader, called Desert Hawk, with the goal to bring the nomads on their side. After the Desert Hawk began questioning the actions of the Nazis, Otto imprisoned him and forced his daughter to tell Allied soldiers that his father was killed by said soldiers while riding alone with his daughter, or else he would be killed. The daughter, Sheilah, later met Sgt. Fury, but instead of telling him the forced lie, she told him the truth, that her mother was killed by Nazis, and that her father was captured by Otto. Some of Otto's nomads later captured Dum-Dum-Dugan, who first tried to escape, and brought him to the colonel. After he ordered that Dugan must be interrogated, Otto went into an underground bunker where he tried to convince the bound nomad leader, Ben Ali Mussim, that his daughter was captured by Allied soldiers, which Ali, to Otto's anger, didn't believed. Unknown to them, Sgt. Fury, his Howling Commando, Hashim and Sheila raided the camp, where Fury tried to convince the nomads, with the translation of Hashim, that the Nazis were actually the bad guys. Otto gave Fury an offer, in which Fury agreed to. Both Fury and Otto got a rifle and a horse, and tried to shoot the other person, who lived after that, told the truth. Otto was shot, but not by Fury, but of Hashim, who couldn't see the "traitorous snake". Otto only got wounded by the shot, and was then given to the Allied forces as a prisoner.

He worked on his newest plan, "The Invasion of England", before his base in the Bavarian Alps was bombed by Sgt. Fury and his Howling Commandos. Fury fought against the remaining Nazis. In the end, he was captured and handed over to the Brits.

otto kronsteig.name: Otto Kronsteig
otto kronsteig.species: Human enhanced by the Shaper of Worlds
otto kronsteig.origin: Otto Kronsteig was one of Adolf Hitler's most brilliant scientists, during which time he apparently developed a means to extend his life span. Upon the Nazis' defeat, Kronsteig fled Germany, eventually seeking refuge in Dr. Doom's Latveria, where he helped Doom create a size-reduction ray. Fearing his assistant would ultimately attempt a coup d'etat, Doom tested the finished ray on Kronsteig himself. Shrinking into a "Microverse", Kronsteig arrived at the planetoid Moto ruled by the reality-altering Shaper of Worlds who, tired of bringing the slug-like inhabitants' dreams to life, fulfilled Kronsteig's dream of a Nazi-invaded USA by turning the Motons into human beings, creating a war-torn Manhattan, and installing Kronsteig as Führer on Wall Street; however, shrunk by Ant-Man (Henry Pym)'s serum, the Hulk arrived on Moto as well and opposed Kronsteig. Based on dreams of a genetic surgery-enhanced Nazi super-being taken from Kronsteig's mind, the Shaper transformed Kronsteig into Captain Axis. When the Hulk fought Axis to a standstill, Kronsteig noted that he could never dream of being put to such a challenge. Since the Shaper could not maintain what could not be dreamed, Axis reverted back to Kronsteig. The Shaper departed soon after, returning Moto to normal and apparently stranding Kronsteig there.
abilities: Genius-Level Intellect: Kronsteig has a genius level intellect. Hand-to-Hand Combat: Thanks to the powers and knowledge granted to him by the Shaper of Worlds, is a formidable hand to hand combatant.

otto mink.name: Otto Mink
otto mink.origin: Otto Mink was a smuggler active in the first half of the 20th Century. Howard Stark used Mink's services to smuggle himself back into New York City after he fled the country when he was accused of selling weapons to enemies of the United States. However, Mink's henchmen tried to extort more money out of Stark's associates Peggy Carter and Edwin Jarvis. This led to a fight breaking out, where Carter not only beat Mink's men but also recovered Stark without giving over any money. Otto Mink was furious at his henchmen's failure, and executed them with his unique automatic pistol. Mink, determined to get teach a lesson to Stark's associates, infiltrated the Griffith Hotel to kill Peggy Carter. The boarding house's supervisor, Miriam Fry, refused to let Mink past the first floor to Carter's room in compliance with the Griffiths' policies, so he snuck up to her floor by crawling through the building's air vents. Before he could break into Peggy's room, he was confronted by her neighbor Dottie Underwood, who showed a bizarre fascination with Mink's gun. Dottie, who was secretly one of Leviathan's assassins, killed Mink by breaking his neck to get possession of the gun. She dragged Mink's corpse back to her room, and hid it under her bed.

fields.notes: Gregory Sporleder portrays Otto Mink in the Marvel's Agent Carter episode "The Blitzkrieg Button."

otto murdo.name: Otto Murdo
otto murdo.origin: Dr. Otto Murdo is a mad genius who is bent on world dominion. To this end, from his secret laboratory, he invented an army of robots. He also began stealing all available radium to power a death ray he hoped to use to take over the world. His plot failed when he made the mistake of stealing a radium sample given to Joel and Josh Williams, brothers who invented the symbiote-based robot known as Flexo. Using a radium detector, they tracked Murdo's lab and unleashed Flexo upon his robot guards. After making short work of the robots, Flexo attacked Murdo and his men. When Murdo's men fired upon the apparent robot, Flexo underwent a monstrous transformation and devoured them. thumb|left|Flexo kills Otto and his henchmen. The Williams brothers later lied that the henchmen's bullets had unleashed a powerful knockout gas, incapacitating Murdo and his men; and that they had contacted the authorities and that Murdo and his men had been arrested.
abilities: Murdo is a scientific genius who invented robot guardians and a death ray powered by radium.
